supporters.quote: hippocampal segmentation volumes did not differentiate between HC and mdaMCI groups. ... Uncorrected vertex-wise surface analysis revealed very little difference in whole brain cortical thickness between HC and mdaMCI. (p.1466/9) ... Whole-brain ROI-to-ROI analysis revealed a significant, global decoupling of the frontal-temporal and temporal-occipital regions in mdaMCI compared to HC. (p.1466/9)
supporters.note: Broadhouse et al. 2021, Sunshine Coast (Australia) local sample, HC n=24, longitudinally confirmed multi-domain amnestic MCI n=14, mild AD n=6; cross-sectional imaging. Resting-state functional connectivity separated mdaMCI from controls where hippocampal subvolumes and cortical thickness did not. Very small MCI group; authors call the findings preliminary and state they cannot conclude about prediction of conversion (p.1470). 'Precedes' is an inference from a cross-sectional contrast. Supports detection where volume is non-discriminative, in this sample only.

supporters.quote: the combined CA1-CA2 mu and volume ROC curve had a larger AUC of 0.85 [95 % CI: 0.75-0.94], compared to the individual mu (AUC = 0.71 [95 % CI: 0.56-0.85]) and volume (AUC = 0.77 [95 % CI: 0.64-0.90]) ROC curves (p.5) ... In the high DG-CA3 volume group, a quadratic regression found that lower DG-CA3 mu was significantly, nonlinearly associated with a higher predicted probability of aMCI classification (p.6) ... Volume: HC 7.65 vs 6.88, p = 0.001, Cohen's d 1.01; all subfield volumes differed (Table 2, p.4)
supporters.note: Delgorio et al. 2023, Delaware, 63 CN and 20 aMCI, MR elastography of hippocampal subfields, cross-sectional. Volume was NOT preserved or non-discriminative: every hippocampal subfield volume differed between groups with larger effect sizes than stiffness, and volume alone (AUC 0.77) beat stiffness alone (AUC 0.71). What the paper does show is that stiffness adds information beyond volume and remains associated with aMCI probability within the above-mean DG-CA3 volume subgroup. Supports 'mechanical measures add to volume and detect aMCI in part of the high-volume regime', not 'volume is late or insufficient'. The record's 'B=-0.11' is the LOW-volume group coefficient, not the high-volume one.

supporters.quote: T2 heterogeneity in CA1-3 and entorhinal cortex and volume of entorhinal cortex showed some ability to predict cognitive decline, where absolute T2 could not, however further studies are required to verify this result. (p.1) ... EC volume was entered as sole predictor of greater cognitive decline in the volume model (beta EC = 0.595, p = .030). However the full model was not statistically significant (p.6)
supporters.note: Wearn et al. 2021, Bristol, 99 HC and 49 MCI (20 followed up at one year). The 'where ... could not' contrast is with ABSOLUTE T2, not with volume; entorhinal volume predicted decline about as well as T2 heterogeneity, and neither overall model was significant. The paper does not report MCI detection in a regime of preserved volume, nor conversion. The claim that T2 heterogeneity precedes atrophy rests on a path model whose direction was fixed a priori (volumes 'were not allowed to predict T2', p.4), in healthy controls. The record's paraphrase ('predicts memory decline where absolute T2 did not') is accurate but is not evidence for the VF-20 statement about volume.

supporters.quote: Neither aMCI, g = -0.22, p = 0.095, 95% CI [-0.48, 0.05], nor naMCI, g = -0.17, p = 0.24 ... had significantly smaller brain or cortical volume compared with NC. (p.5) ... Compared with NC, both aMCI, g = -0.84, p < 0.001, 95% CI [-1.01, -0.68], and naMCI, g = -0.28, p = 0.002 ... had significantly smaller medial temporal lobe volume. (p.5) ... for aMCI, we detected a large difference in medial temporal lobe volume in the context of small differences in total brain volume (p.13)
supporters.note: Yeung et al. 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis of 50 studies comparing aMCI, naMCI and NC. The whole-brain result the record cites is correct, but the same meta-analysis finds medial temporal lobe/hippocampal volume the largest and most consistent aMCI abnormality (g=-0.84, 26 of 29 studies), larger than pooled metabolic (g=-0.76, marginal) or cortical thickness (g=-0.77, marginal) effects. It therefore contradicts the 'especially hippocampal' part of the statement, and it does not test any non-volumetric measure in a regime of preserved volume. Evidence is cross-sectional. It is also a synthesis, not an independent primary dataset, and may overlap with primary studies in the corpus (it includes a Broadhouse 2019 study from the same group as P-518).

supporters.quote: Plasma Abeta42/40, p-tau217, and tau PET each conferred higher risk, while hippocampal volume did not. (p.2) ... By contrast, the effects of MEG alpha power (LRT = 3.78; p(FDR) = 0.0623) and hippocampal volume (LRT = 3.18, p(FDR) = 0.0744) did not survive correction. (p.10) ... Higher alpha power was associated with increased short-term risk of progression (main effect log(HR) = 1.13, HR = 3.08, p = 0.0052), but this association weakened over time (p.13)
supporters.note: Gallego-Rudolf et al. 2025, medRxiv PREPRINT (not peer reviewed), PREVENT-AD, 102 cognitively unimpaired adults with family history of AD, 31 progressed to MCI over mean 5.9 years. Hippocampal volume did not significantly improve prediction of CU-to-MCI, but neither did MEG alpha power as a fixed effect; alpha became informative only as a time-varying effect. The robust predictors were proteinopathy markers (plasma Abeta42/40, p-tau217, amyloid and tau PET), which are molecular, not functional, microstructural, mechanical or metabolic. Hippocampal volume was retained in the final stepwise model (p=0.066). Supports 'hippocampal volume non-predictive for CU-to-MCI in this cohort' and 'functional MEG adds time-varying information', not the full statement.

supporters.quote: Concerning HVF, the analysis revealed a significantly lower survival time (median 1305 days ...) for MCI N+ compared to N- (median 2514 days ...). The log-rank test showed significant differences ... (chi-square = 13.009; P value < 0.001). (p.7) ... The log rank (Mantel-Cox) analysis performed to compare the N+ curves showed that only the PerpPD+ signature curve was significantly different compared to cortical volume fraction (chi-square = 4.051; P value < 0.05). No other significant difference was found in the comparison between curves. (p.7-8)
supporters.note: Torso et al. 2025, NACC, 826 participants of whom 196 MCI in the survival analysis; MCI-to-dementia progression; authors are employees/co-founder of Oxford Brain Diagnostics, which holds the patent on the diffusivity method. Hippocampal volume was itself a significant predictor of conversion and differed between MCI converters and non-converters (Table 1), so volume was not preserved or non-discriminative. PerpPD+ positives had a shorter median survival, but the pairwise test did not show PerpPD+ significantly different from hippocampal volume or cortical thickness; it beat only cortical volume fraction. The record's 'outperforms hippocampal/cortical volume and thickness in survival' holds only for median survival time, not for a significant pairwise difference. Dichotomised measures.

narrowed_wording: In small single-cohort studies, non-volumetric measures carried information that volume did not: resting-state connectivity separated confirmed multi-domain amnestic MCI from controls where hippocampal subvolumes did not (P-518), hippocampal-subfield stiffness added to subfield volume in classifying amnestic MCI, including within the higher-volume subgroup (P-478), and in a preprint hippocampal volume did not significantly predict progression from normal cognition to MCI while temporal MEG alpha power carried time-varying risk (P-584); a cortical diffusivity signature predicted MCI-to-dementia conversion at least as well as hippocampal volume (P-581). Hippocampal volume nonetheless remained discriminative for amnestic MCI in most of these samples.
reasoning: As stated in Table A1 ('volumetric atrophy is a comparatively late and insufficient MCI marker ... measures detect MCI or predict conversion where volume is preserved'), only P-518 answers yes, and it is a 14-patient cross-sectional contrast. Two supporters do not support it: P-432 compares T2 heterogeneity with absolute T2, not with volume, and entorhinal volume predicted decline as well as T2 heterogeneity (neither model significant); P-460 confirms the whole-brain null but reports hippocampal/MTL atrophy as the largest aMCI effect (g=-0.84), which contradicts the 'especially hippocampal' clause. Three are partial: in P-478 and P-581 hippocampal volume was itself significantly discriminative/prognostic (in P-478 it beat stiffness alone; in P-581 PerpPD+ was not significantly better than hippocampal volume), so they show complementarity or parity, not insufficiency of volume in a volume-preserved regime; P-584 (a preprint) shows hippocampal volume non-predictive for CU-to-MCI, but MEG alpha also failed as a fixed effect and the robust predictors were molecular proteinopathy markers outside the named families. The stated form therefore fails. A narrower form, that non-volumetric functional, mechanical and microstructural measures carry information beyond or comparable to hippocampal volume, is supported by P-518, P-478 and P-584 (with P-581 as parity evidence), across four method families (rs-fMRI, MRE, MEG, cortical diffusion) and four datasets (Sunshine Coast, Delaware, PREVENT-AD, NACC), so it clears the three-supporter rule. Recommended changes: drop P-432 and P-460 as supporters, drop 'late and insufficient' and the whole-brain clause, flag P-584 as a preprint, correct the record's P-478 coefficient (B=-0.11 is the low-volume group) and its P-581 'outperforms' wording. The record's 'adversarially source-verified; grounding_ok=true' did not survive reading the sources in full.
